punchline: An 'overnight success' is usually just the day outsiders noticed a flywheel that had been turning for years.
thirty_sec: In Good to Great, Jim Collins asked leaders of companies that went from good to great to name the moment everything changed. Most couldn't, because there wasn't one. Their success came from pushing a heavy flywheel in the same direction until momentum took over. Outsiders saw a sudden breakthrough. Insiders saw steady buildup. Meanwhile, the companies that stayed merely good kept launching flashy new programs and reversing course, so they never built momentum.
question: Think of the thing you're proudest of. Was there really one moment that made it happen, or was it a long run of small pushes?
